title: A Coprimality Topology on the Gaussian Integers: Kolmogorov Quotient and Gaussian Prime Density
headline: Coprimality Topology on Gaussian Integers: Kolmogorov Quotient and Prime Density
tldr: We introduce a topology on non‑zero Gaussian integers where basic open sets consist of elements coprime to a fixed Gaussian integer. By examining prime supports, we identify indistinguishable points, prove hyperconnectedness, and compute the density of Gaussian primes in this topological space.
significance: This work links number theory with topological concepts, offering new insights into the structure of Gaussian integers and their prime distribution.

title: Squarefree Matrix Formulas for the CWR Invariant of Alternating Knots and Links
headline: Squarefree Matrix Formulas for CWR Invariant of Alternating Knots
tldr: We present weighted-matrix formulas that compute the components of the CWR invariant for oriented non-split alternating links. By attaching independent commuting variables to each vertex of a consolidated Tait graph and extracting the squarefree part of the trace, we isolate simple cycles, yielding a uniform construction for all k.
significance: These formulas provide a unified algebraic framework for computing higher-order CWR invariants, advancing the study of knot invariants in low-dimensional topology.

title: Phonon spectral functions of low-density polaron metals
headline: First Low-Density Polaron Metal Phonon Spectra via DMRG Reveal Electron-Phonon Coupling Effects
tldr: Using DMRG, we computed phonon spectral functions for a one-dimensional Holstein model at low carrier densities (x ≤ 0.15). The results show how electron‑phonon coupling λ shapes the low‑energy excitations, providing the first benchmark data in this regime.
significance: These findings offer a critical benchmark for theoretical models of polaronic metals and guide future experimental investigations of low‑density electron‑phonon systems.

title: On generalised d'Alembert-type integral representations for damped wave equations on the quarter-plane
headline: Generalized d'Alembert Integral Solutions for Damped Wave Equations on the Quarter-Plane
tldr: The paper derives closed-form integral representations for the damped wave equation on a quarter-plane with general initial and boundary data. It rigorously verifies these solutions in classical function spaces, extending the d'Alembert method to hyperbolic heat and telegrapher equations.
significance: It provides a unified analytic framework that simplifies the analysis of damped wave phenomena in engineering and physics.

title: CalibForge: Adversarial Solver Calibration for Scaling Learnable Terminal Tasks
headline: CalibForge: Automating Task Synthesis with Verified Solver Calibration for Agent Learning
tldr: CalibForge automatically generates terminal tasks that are not only solvable but also appropriately challenging by calibrating tasks against solver performance. It uses verified solver behavior to iteratively revise candidate tasks, enabling scalable training of learnable agents.
significance: This approach enables efficient scaling of agent training by ensuring tasks are both executable and optimally challenging, reducing wasted effort on trivial or infeasible problems.

title: Vector Edge Solitons and Domain Walls in a Nonlinear Mechanical Topological Insulator
headline: Nonlinear Edge Solitons and Domain Walls in a Mechanical Topological Insulator
tldr: We demonstrate that nonlinear interactions between edge modes in a 2D mechanical topological insulator can be captured by a coupled nonlinear Schrödinger equation, leading to stable soliton-like waves and domain walls. These findings provide a new platform for exploring topological phenomena in nonlinear mechanical systems.
significance: This work bridges nonlinear dynamics and topological physics, opening avenues for robust waveguiding and information processing in mechanical metamaterials.

title: Distributed coordination for transmission-distribution systems with nonlinear flexibility aggregation
headline: Optimizing Transmission-Distribution Coordination with Nonlinear Flexibility Aggregation for DER-Rich Networks
tldr: This paper proposes a scalable method for aggregating distribution-level flexibility using nonlinear models, addressing misclassifications inherent in linear approaches. It demonstrates improved feasibility and cost-efficiency in multi-period integrated transmission-distribution coordination.
significance: It enables more accurate and efficient integration of high DER penetration into grid operations, reducing operational costs and enhancing reliability.

title: Scalable estimation of VARMA models
headline: Scalable Estimation of VARMA Models: A New Efficient Likelihood Approach
tldr: We present a scalable algorithm for estimating VARMA models that overcomes non-convexity and high dimensionality. The method achieves comparable accuracy to full likelihood while reducing computational cost dramatically.
significance: This work enables practical use of VARMA models in high-dimensional time-series analysis, improving forecasting accuracy with fewer parameters.

title: Circular sorting in the alternating group
headline: Circular Sorting in the Alternating Group: Max Adjacent Swaps on a Circle
tldr: Researchers Adin, Alon, and Roichman derived a formula for the maximum number of adjacent swaps needed to sort n points arranged on a circle. This result connects the problem to the number of adjacent transpositions required to transform any permutation in the alternating group.
significance: The formula provides a precise bound for circular sorting, enriching our understanding of permutation sorting complexity in group theory.

title: A Regression-Based Framework for the ACF, PACF, Durbin-Levinson Recursion, and One-Step-Ahead Prediction
headline: Unified Regression Framework for ACF, PACF, Durbin–Levinson, and One-Step Prediction
tldr: This note presents a regression-based approach to derive the autocorrelation function, partial autocorrelation, and Durbin–Levinson recursion, linking them to familiar linear regression concepts. It also demonstrates how to use this framework for efficient one-step-ahead forecasting.
significance: By framing these classic time‑series tools within regression, the article makes them more accessible to students and practitioners, bridging a conceptual gap.

title: Benchmarking the Benchmarks: Evaluating Benchmarks for Conversational Agents
headline: Assessing Benchmark Quality for Task-Oriented Conversational Agents
tldr: We propose a reference-free framework that uses LLM judges to evaluate benchmark consistency, complexity, and policy coverage for task-oriented conversational agents. This approach reveals flaws in existing benchmarks and offers a scalable, automated assessment method.
significance: Reliable benchmark evaluation is essential for advancing conversational AI, and our framework provides the first systematic, automated way to audit benchmark quality.

title: Global weak solutions to the Cahn-Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility and singular diffusion
headline: Weak Solutions for Cahn-Hilliard with Degenerate Mobility and Singular Diffusion
tldr: The paper establishes existence of global weak solutions for a Cahn-Hilliard equation with degenerate mobility and singular diffusion. The analysis is carried out in three-dimensional convex domains, extending previous results.
significance: It advances mathematical understanding of phase separation models relevant to polymer blends.

title: Investigating Artificial Intelligence Digital Sovereignty in Mobile Shopping Apps: A Case Study of Nigeria
headline: AI in Nigerian Mobile Shopping Apps: Assessing Digital Sovereignty and Platform Transparency
tldr: This study explores how AI-driven features in Nigerian e‑commerce apps influence users' digital sovereignty, focusing on transparency and control. Findings highlight gaps in platform accountability and suggest policy measures to safeguard consumer autonomy.
significance: Understanding AI's impact on digital sovereignty is crucial for protecting Nigerian consumers from opaque algorithmic practices.

title: Structured coherence: A modern perspective on optical coherence as a resource
headline: Optical Coherence as a Modern Resource: From Theory to Practical Discrete Modes
tldr: Optical coherence traditionally relies on continuous spatial and temporal correlation functions, yet real-world applications only access discrete degrees of freedom. This paper reinterprets coherence as a resource, enabling deterministic mode exploitation in practical optical systems.
significance: It bridges fundamental coherence theory with actionable strategies for engineering optical devices in discrete settings.

title: A Master-Salve Robot Manipulator for Needle-Based Teleoperation in MRI Chamber
headline: MR‑Safe Master‑Slave Robot Enables Precise Needle Teleoperation Inside MRI Scanners
tldr: We developed an MR‑safe master‑slave robotic system that allows surgeons to steer a needle inside an MRI chamber using a fluid‑coupled 2+1‑DoF master and slave. The system provides multimodal control and real‑time force feedback, improving precision for abdominal interventions.
significance: This platform enables safe, high‑precision needle interventions in MRI environments, potentially improving outcomes for image‑guided therapies.

title: Resourced Authority A Mechanism-Design Model for Participatory Governance of Deployed AI Agents
headline: Resourced Authority: A Mechanism-Design Model for Continuous AI Governance Through Compute Budgets
tldr: We propose a mechanism design framework that uses compute budgets to enforce authorization for deployed AI agents, enabling continuous participatory governance. By treating compute as a governance lever, the model aligns AI behavior with safety objectives while allowing stakeholders to adjust resource allocation in real time.
significance: This approach offers a scalable, self-enforcing method to ensure AI agents remain aligned with human values without requiring constant oversight.

title: Challenges in Evaluating Explanation Methods for Static and Evolving Data
headline: Evaluating XAI: Human‑Grounded Tests and Adaptive Explanations in Image Recognition
tldr: The paper critiques current XAI evaluation practices, using DetoxAI to highlight bias detection and concept unlearning gaps. It demonstrates a human‑grounded assessment of image‑classification explanations and proposes adaptive methods to improve explanation quality.
significance: It underscores the need for rigorous, human‑centered evaluation frameworks to ensure trustworthy AI explanations in visual tasks.

title: Clump Migration in Disk Galaxies: Revisiting Chandrasekhar's Dynamical Friction
headline: Reassessing Dynamical Friction: Clump Migration in Disk Galaxies and Bulge Growth
tldr: We test Chandrasekhar’s dynamical friction against N‑body simulations of massive clumps in realistic disk galaxies. The classic formula overestimates inspiral times by up to a factor of two, indicating the need for revised models.
significance: Accurate clump inspiral times are essential for understanding bulge formation and the secular evolution of disk galaxies.

title: RP-OPSD: Reasoning-Pivot-Guided On-Policy Self-Distillation for Multilingual Reasoning Transfer
headline: Reasoning-Pivot Guided Self-Distillation Enhances Multilingual LLM Reasoning for Cross-Language Transfer
tldr: The paper introduces RP-OPSD, a self-distillation framework that prioritizes reasoning signals to improve multilingual reasoning in LLMs. It demonstrates that guiding distillation with reasoning pivots yields better cross-lingual transfer than existing methods.
significance: It offers a new way to extend reasoning capabilities of LLMs to low-resource languages.

title: TRAJDEBUG: Tracing Error Lifecycle to Identify Critical Failures in Long-Horizon Agent Trajectories
headline: Tracing Early Errors in Long-Horizon LLM Agent Trajectories with TRAJDEBUG
tldr: TRAJDEBUG introduces a method to pinpoint the earliest error step causing failure in long agent trajectories, enabling targeted debugging of LLM-based systems. It leverages error lifecycle analysis to improve reliability in complex, multi-step tasks.
significance: This work provides a systematic approach to reduce cascading failures in autonomous agents, enhancing safety and robustness.

title: Dimension-Free Polylogarithmic Quantum Shadow Tomography from Sequential Pretty-Good Measurements
headline: New Dimension-Free Polylogarithmic Quantum Shadow Tomography Achieves Efficient Expectation Estimation
tldr: The paper presents a quantum shadow tomography algorithm that scales polylogarithmically with dimension, eliminating the curse of dimensionality. It uses sequential pretty-good measurements to estimate all expectation values with high probability and additive accuracy ε.
significance: This breakthrough enables practical quantum state characterization for high-dimensional systems, paving the way for scalable quantum technologies.

title: Learning When to Trust via Selective Context Preference Optimization
headline: Selective Trust in LLMs: Optimizing Context Preference for Reliable Answers
tldr: This paper introduces MIST, a benchmark that tests language models' ability to selectively trust contextual signals. By optimizing context preference, models can avoid misleading cues while still leveraging useful information.
significance: It provides a framework to balance robustness and usefulness in LLMs, addressing a key failure mode in current models.

title: A Tale of Two Compact Bosons
headline: Neural Network Field Theory Unifies Compact Bosons via Mixed Latent Variables
tldr: Neural network field theory (NN-FT) models field theories using network architectures and latent variable distributions, extending to compact theories by summing over discrete topological sectors. The paper applies this mixed continuous/discrete latent-variable construction to two compact boson models, illustrating the framework’s power.
significance: This work bridges machine learning and quantum field theory, offering a novel, data-driven approach to studying topologically nontrivial compact bosonic systems.

title: $ω$-0: A Latent Predictive World Action Model for Concurrent Humanoid Loco-Manipulation
headline: ω-0: Unified Latent Predictive Model for Concurrent Humanoid Locomotion and Manipulation
tldr: The paper introduces ω-0, a latent predictive world-action model that jointly learns locomotion, posture, balance, and manipulation for humanoid robots. By integrating whole-body dynamics into a single latent space, ω-0 enables real-time coordinated behavior, outperforming prior decomposed policies.
significance: ω-0 bridges the gap between separate locomotion and manipulation modules, enabling more natural and efficient humanoid task execution.

title: DyPES-VLA: Learning Shared Dynamics Priors and Embodiment-Specific Control for Cross-Embodiment Manipulation
headline: DyPES-VLA: Shared Dynamics Priors for Cross-Embodiment Robot Manipulation
tldr: DyPES-VLA introduces a framework that learns shared dynamics priors across diverse robot embodiments while tailoring control policies to each embodiment. This approach improves cross-embodiment transfer and reduces the need for extensive manual data collection.
significance: By leveraging shared dynamics priors, DyPES-VLA enables more efficient and scalable training of vision-language-action models for heterogeneous robots, accelerating deployment in real-world manipulation tasks.

title: The Bitter Lesson of Tool Calling
headline: Evaluating Tool Calling in LLMs: A Benchmark for Code-Capable Models
tldr: Tool calling turns LLMs into agents that can act beyond their training data. Yet, no systematic benchmark exists to evaluate code-based tool use across model generations in real-world tasks.
significance: This study provides the first comprehensive benchmark for tool calling in LLMs, guiding future model development.

title: Tracing the Heart: An Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart-Failure Feature Engineering
headline: Tracing the Heart: Building an Evidence-Linked Pipeline for Heart‑Failure EHR Feature Engineering
tldr: EHR feature engineering consumes nearly half of data scientists’ effort, especially for heart failure. This paper presents a rule‑based and LLM‑augmented pipeline that links guideline‑driven reasoning to structured data, accelerating model development.
significance: By automating feature extraction, the pipeline reduces bottlenecks and enables faster, evidence‑based heart‑failure research.

title: An Optimal Agnostic PAC Algorithm
headline: Optimal Agnostic PAC Learning for Finite VC Classes
tldr: The paper introduces an algorithm that achieves the statistically optimal risk bound for any hypothesis class with finite VC dimension, matching the minimax lower bound up to constant factors.
significance: It provides the first practical learner that attains the best possible error rate in agnostic learning settings.

title: AV-AIVAT: 74x Cheaper Agent Evaluation with Certified Anytime-Valid Stopping in Imperfect-Information Games
headline: AV-AIVAT Cuts Agent Evaluation Cost 74× with Anytime-Valid Stopping in Games
tldr: AV-AIVAT introduces a statistically sound anytime-valid stopping rule that dramatically reduces the number of games required to compare agents in imperfect-information settings. The method achieves a 74× cost reduction while maintaining rigorous confidence guarantees, making large-scale agent benchmarking more affordable and reliable.
significance: This breakthrough enables rapid, cost-effective evaluation of AI agents, accelerating research and deployment in strategic games and beyond.

title: The Low Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
headline: Low-Frequency Trap: Video Language Models Fail at Simple Event Bookkeeping
tldr: Video language models struggle to accurately count and timestamp low-frequency events because existing benchmarks conflate event count, rate, duration, and visual complexity. We propose a trace‑grounded parametric benchmark that audits reported events against executable ground truth, isolating failure modes.
significance: This work provides a clearer diagnostic tool for improving video language models, enabling more reliable event detection in real-world applications.

title: PyOMES: an open-source framework for biochemical process modelling
headline: PyOMES: Open-Source Framework for Dynamic Biochemical Process Modelling
tldr: PyOMES is a Python-based, open-source environment that simplifies dynamic and steady-state biochemical process modelling through a modular, generalized framework. It supports a wide range of biological, chemical, and biochemical systems under a single, accessible platform.
significance: By providing a unified, modular toolkit, PyOMES accelerates research and development across diverse biochemical engineering domains.

title: Universality in random graphs via optimal linking systems: trees and beyond
headline: Random Graphs Achieve Universal Tree Embedding
tldr: Researchers prove that a sparse random graph with edge probability C ln n/n contains every bounded-degree tree on n vertices. This resolves a question posed by Montgomery and advances our understanding of universality in random graphs.
significance: It establishes a tight threshold for embedding all bounded-degree trees, a fundamental problem in graph theory.

title: The QCD Axion and Neutrino Masses
headline: Linking the QCD Axion to Neutrino Masses: A Unified BSM Insight
tldr: The Peccei-Quinn mechanism solves the strong CP problem by predicting the QCD axion, while neutrino masses hint at new physics. We investigate a framework where both phenomena arise from a common underlying symmetry, offering testable predictions.
significance: This work proposes a novel unification of two major BSM puzzles, potentially guiding future experiments in axion searches and neutrino physics.

title: CoCo-IR: Contextual Composed Image Retrieval
headline: CoCo-IR: Enabling Iterative Contextual Composed Image Retrieval for Complex Visual Searches
tldr: We introduce CoCo-IR, a novel task that allows users to iteratively refine image search results through contextual interactions. Our approach leverages instruction-based retrieval and demonstrates improved performance over single-turn systems.
significance: CoCo-IR addresses the limitation of single-turn retrieval, enabling more natural and effective visual search experiences.

title: Reasoning Core: Designing Broad Procedural Data for Completion-Supervised Reasoning Training
headline: Reasoning Core: 50 Procedural Generators for Training LLMs in AI Research
tldr: We present Reasoning Core, a suite of 50 procedural generators covering math, logic, planning, and more, enabling scalable, verifiable reasoning data for completion-supervised fine-tuning. Each generator includes semantic scoring, difficulty knobs, and task evaluators to support robust LLM training.
significance: Reasoning Core provides the first large, open-source benchmark of procedurally generated reasoning tasks, accelerating LLM development.

title: Fast Quantum Interconnects via Neutral Atom Ensembles
headline: Fast Quantum Interconnects via Neutral Atom Ensembles for Scalable Quantum Computing
tldr: We present a scalable quantum interconnect that generates remote entanglement at rates compatible with current neutral-atom processors, leveraging strong dipole-dipole interactions between Rydberg states. This approach promises high-rate entanglement distribution essential for scalable quantum computing.
significance: This work enables high-speed entanglement distribution, bridging the gap between local gate operations and long-distance quantum communication.

title: Objects as Audio-Visual Modal Sound Fields
headline: Integrating Impact Sounds into 3D Reconstruction for Material and Structural Insight
tldr: Modern 3D reconstruction focuses on geometry but neglects acoustic cues. By modeling impact sounds, we can infer material properties and structural integrity without costly simulations or massive datasets.
significance: This approach enables richer, physics-informed scene understanding by combining visual and auditory data.

title: Argus: A General-Purpose Agentic Runtime for Long-Horizon Reasoning
headline: Argus: A Persistent Agentic Runtime Framework for Long-Horizon AI Reasoning
tldr: Argus is a self‑evolving runtime that lets AI agents persist with a current approach when evidence supports it, but pivot when measurements indicate failure or hidden constraints. It orchestrates Manager, Planner, Engineer, and Reviewer components to execute bounded missions over durable project state, enabling robust long‑horizon reasoning.
significance: Argus advances long‑horizon AI by providing a modular, persistent runtime that balances stability and adaptability, crucial for complex, multi‑step tasks.

title: OctoLong: Mid-Training On Cross-Repository Code Contexts Enhances Long-Context Modeling
headline: OctoLong Boosts Long-Context Language Models During Cross-Repository Code Training for
tldr: OctoLong introduces a mid-training strategy that leverages cross-repository code contexts to improve long-context modeling in language models. By exposing models to diverse, long-distance dependencies across codebases, it enhances in-context learning and agentic workflows.
significance: This approach expands the effective training corpus for long-context LMs, enabling more robust reasoning over extended sequences.

title: Toward Skill-Native LLMs: Skill Entropy for Benchmarking and Training Long-Horizon Reasoning
headline: Skill Entropy: Benchmarking Cross-Skill Long-Horizon Reasoning in LLMs
tldr: Researchers introduce skill entropy as a metric to evaluate how well large language models switch between distinct reasoning skills in multi-step tasks. The framework also guides training to improve long-horizon problem solving.
significance: It provides a systematic way to assess and enhance LLMs' ability to handle complex, multi-skill reasoning.

title: Teaching Nemotron Greek: Mining a Corpus, Adapting Retrieval, and Grounding Generation for Modern Greek across Specialist Domains
headline: Adapting Nemotron Retrieval for Modern Greek: Corpus Mining, Synthetic Supervision, and RAG
tldr: We extend NVIDIA’s Nemotron retrieval stack to Modern Greek by mining a large multilingual corpus, generating synthetic supervision, and training a retrieval model that improves retrieval-augmented generation in legal, energy, financial, and medical domains. The resulting open-source benchmark demonstrates significant gains over existing multilingual models.
significance: This work fills a critical gap in multilingual retrieval, enabling high-quality RAG for Greek-speaking professionals across specialized sectors.

title: SmartMage: Dynamic Modality Orchestration for 3D Scene Understanding
headline: SmartMage: Adaptive Modality Switching for Real‑Time 3D Scene Understanding with Large Language Models
tldr: SmartMage introduces a dynamic modality orchestration framework that selects the most relevant visual and geometric cues for each query, enabling more accurate 3D scene understanding. By integrating multimodal large language models with adaptive sensor fusion, it outperforms fixed‑modality baselines on benchmark tasks.
significance: This work demonstrates that query‑dependent modality selection can substantially improve multimodal reasoning in embodied AI, paving the way for more efficient and context‑aware perception systems.

title: The Loss Does Not See the Basis, but Adam Does
headline: Gradient Descent's Low-Rank Bias vs Adam: The Role of Gauge Symmetry in Factored Models
tldr: When training factored models, gradient descent naturally favors low-rank solutions due to gauge-equivariant dynamics, whereas Adam lacks this bias. The difference stems from the loss's invariance under simultaneous rotations of U and V, affecting how optimizers explore the parameter space.
significance: Understanding this bias informs optimizer choice for efficient training of large-scale matrix factorization tasks.

title: Near-Field Velocity Estimation and Doppler-Aware Localization in OFDM Massive MIMO
headline: Doppler-Aware Near-Field Localization in OFDM Massive MIMO: Low-Complexity Recursive Estimation
tldr: Target motion in OFDM massive MIMO creates antenna-dependent Doppler shifts that degrade near-field localization if ignored. This paper introduces a low-complexity recursive framework that jointly estimates velocity and localization, improving accuracy.
significance: Accurate near-field localization in massive MIMO systems is critical for high-resolution sensing and communication, and this work provides a practical method to mitigate Doppler-induced errors.

title: ParVL: Parallel Scaling and Expandable Compute Allocation for Multimodal LLMs
headline: ParVL: Parallel Scaling for Multimodal LLMs with Dynamic Compute Allocation
tldr: ParVL introduces a parallel scaling framework that allows separate, task‑specific allocation of compute resources between vision and language modules in multimodal LLMs. This reduces memory and latency overhead while enabling flexible, efficient inference across diverse applications.
significance: By decoupling vision and language compute budgets, ParVL offers a scalable, low‑latency alternative to monolithic MLLM scaling, facilitating real‑time multimodal AI.

title: WorldCup Arena: Prospective, Leakage-Free Evaluation of Frontier LLMs on a Live Tournament
headline: Live Forecasting: Evaluating LLMs During the 2026 FIFA World Cup
tldr: Researchers tested six cutting‑edge LLMs in real time over the 2026 FIFA World Cup, measuring their predictive accuracy without relying on post‑event data. The study demonstrates a novel, leakage‑free benchmark that captures true forecasting performance.
significance: This work establishes the first live, prospective benchmark for LLM forecasting, revealing how well models generalize to unfolding events.

title: TurnSight: Turn-Level Hindsight Self-Distillation for Tool-Integrated Reasoning
headline: TurnSight: Fine-Grained Self-Distillation Boosts Tool-Integrated Reasoning for Complex Tasks in LLMs
tldr: TurnSight introduces turn-level hindsight self-distillation, providing dense credit signals during iterative tool use. This approach improves long-horizon reasoning in large language models without requiring trajectory-level supervision.
significance: By enabling fine-grained learning signals, TurnSight advances the efficiency and accuracy of tool-integrated reasoning systems.

title: Calibrating Trustworthiness: Co-Designing Metrics and Visualizations for Evaluating LLMs in Education
headline: Co-Designing Trust Metrics to Evaluate LLMs for Educational Use Effectively
tldr: This study proposes a structured framework for assessing LLM trustworthiness in educational contexts, integrating pedagogical alignment metrics. By co-designing visualizations and benchmarks, it enables educators and developers to identify and mitigate potential disruptions.
significance: It bridges the gap between technical LLM evaluation and pedagogical needs, fostering safer AI integration in learning environments.

title: Localizing polymers promotes the centre-mode elastic instability
headline: Localizing Polymers Amplifies Centre-Mode Elastic Instability in Dilute Solutions
tldr: The centre-mode elastic instability can arise without inertia in dilute polymer flows. This study shows that nonuniform polymer distributions, such as a polymer-laden core between solvent streams, significantly enhance the instability.
significance: Understanding how polymer localization drives instability informs design of microfluidic devices and improves control of polymer processing.

title: Semantic Bundling: Interactive Node and Edge Bundling to Simplify Knowledge Graphs using Large Language Models
headline: Semantic Bundling: Interactive Node and Edge Bundling for Knowledge Graph Simplification with LLMs
tldr: We introduce Semantic Bundling, a visual analytics method that uses large language models to guide interactive node and edge bundling in knowledge graphs, making large corpora easier to interpret. The approach preserves semantic relationships while reducing visual clutter, enabling analysts to explore document collections more efficiently.
significance: Semantic Bundling bridges LLM-driven semantic understanding with graph visualization, offering a scalable solution for interpreting complex knowledge graphs.

title: PAST-Bench: Benchmarking the Foundations of Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal Agents
headline: PAST-Bench: Measuring Recursive Self-Improvement in Personal AI Agents for Future Capabilities
tldr: PAST-Bench evaluates whether personal AI agents can turn their accumulated experience into better future behavior. The benchmark tracks preference retention, task history, tool usage, and skill learning across sessions to systematically test recursive self-improvement.
significance: This work provides the first systematic test of recursive self-improvement in personal agents, offering a foundation for future AI safety and capability research.

title: Test-Time Scaling in Reasoning LLMs: Inference Regimes, Evaluation, and Reproducibility
headline: Test-Time Scaling Boosts Reasoning in Large Language Models by Extending Inference Algorithms
tldr: Large language models can solve harder reasoning tasks by scaling inference time. Various algorithms—trajectory extension, candidate sampling, partial state search—improve performance, but their statistical properties differ.
significance: This work clarifies how inference regimes affect reasoning accuracy, guiding reproducible benchmarking of LLMs.

title: Agogic: Performance-Timed Music Tokens for LLM-Native Text-to-Symbolic-Music Generation
headline: Agogic: Evaluating Music Tokenization Impact on LLM-Based Text-to-Music Generation Across Seven Representations
tldr: The study isolates the effect of music tokenization by swapping representations while keeping the Qwen3.5 model, data, and decoding constant. Results show that token choice significantly alters performance, with some tokenizations approaching the model-free ceiling.
significance: It provides the first quantitative benchmark of tokenization strategies for symbolic music generation, guiding future LLM design.

title: When Attention Goes Blind: Numerical Failure in ALiBi Positional Encodings
headline: Floating-Point Underflow Undermines ALiBi Positional Encoding in Large Language Models
tldr: The study uncovers that ALiBi’s linear bias scaling can underflow floating-point precision, causing many attention weights to zero out and rendering some heads partially blind. It analyzes the impact, proposes four mitigation strategies, and demonstrates the issue in state-of-the-art models.
significance: This finding highlights a critical, previously overlooked vulnerability in a widely used positional encoding technique, affecting the reliability of modern foundation models.

title: WorldExam: Benchmarking World Models from Apparent Appearance to Inherent Reactivity
headline: Benchmarking World Models: From Video Appearance to Inherent Reactivity Evaluation
tldr: Controllable video generation models are being used as world models, requiring evaluation beyond visual fidelity to include the model's ability to infer and generate plausible world reactions. The paper proposes a benchmark that tests both appearance and inherent reactivity of such models.
significance: This benchmark advances the assessment of generative models by incorporating dynamic reasoning, enabling more realistic and useful AI-driven simulations.

title: Discovery of the Distant, Ultra-Faint Milky Way Satellite Aquarius IV with the Vera C. Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2
headline: Discovery of Ultra-Faint Milky Way Satellite Aquarius IV Using Vera C. Rubin Observatory Data
tldr: Astronomers identified Aquarius IV, a faint Milky Way satellite, with 8σ significance in Rubin Observatory Early Data Preview 2 and confirmed it at 6σ using Dark Energy Camera imagery. This marks the first satellite found using Rubin data, expanding our knowledge of the Galaxy’s outskirts.
significance: It demonstrates the Rubin Observatory’s power to uncover extremely faint celestial objects, opening new avenues for studying the Milky Way’s structure.

title: Bridging Artificial Intelligence and Power Systems Education Using a Hands-On Executable Framework
headline: Hands‑On AI Framework Bridges Power Systems Education Gap
tldr: The paper introduces an executable AI framework that makes power system modeling, forecasting, and control accessible to students and interdisciplinary researchers. It provides reusable modules and hands‑on exercises, filling a gap left by specialized, non‑reusable AI studies.
significance: By offering a reusable, hands‑on AI toolkit, the framework democratizes power systems education and accelerates interdisciplinary innovation.

title: VR3D: View-Robust 3D Representation Learning for Aerial-Ground Person Re-Identification
headline: VR3D: Robust 3D Representation for Aerial‑Ground Person Re‑Identification Across Viewpoints
tldr: Aerial‑ground person re‑identification suffers from viewpoint variations causing occlusion and deformation. VR3D introduces a view‑robust 3D representation learning framework that decouples viewpoint bias, improving cross‑platform matching.
significance: By learning view‑invariant 3D features, VR3D enables more reliable person re‑identification between aerial and ground cameras, a critical capability for surveillance and search‑and‑rescue operations.

title: SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper (LVM): Dithered Data Cube Reconstruction with 3dcubegen
headline: Reconstructing SDSS-V LVM Data Cubes: Dithered Observations and 3dcubegen Techniques
tldr: The SDSS-V Local Volume Mapper uses multiple dithered observations to achieve full spatial coverage of nearby galaxies. The 3dcubegen software reconstructs these observations into high-resolution data cubes for scientific analysis.
significance: This approach enhances spatial sampling and spectral depth, enabling unprecedented studies of the Milky Way and nearby galaxies.

title: Staying Productive Under the Palm Trees. On Graded Coeffect Typing in the Tropical Semiring
headline: Modeling Time and Productivity with Graded Coeffect Typing in the Tropical Semiring
tldr: We present a graded coeffect typing system that uses the tropical semiring over natural numbers to model time delays in function parameters. This approach guarantees productivity of well-typed programs while faithfully representing temporal availability of resources.
significance: This work provides a rigorous framework for reasoning about time-dependent resource availability in functional programming, bridging type theory and temporal logic.
